messages.author: 06199470668a2843
messages.subject: Reprise - density estimates and covariates
parts:
Hi everyone,

I was searching through the archives for an answer to a particular
question, and found that it had been asked before but may not have
received an answer at the time. I'm quoting the mail below.

Basically, the question is: can a parameter that has been used in a MCDS
model as a covariate of detection probability later also be used as a
predictor of density in, say, a regression analysis of the resulting
density estimates? Or does this confound the effects of the covariate on
detection probability and density?

If this has been covered before, please point me in the right direction!

cheers
florian

quote:
-----------------

Jeff and others:



Please correct me if I am wrong. I am sending the following comments and
question because I am new to distance sampling and want to learn more.



I think the best estimates of density will be those from the best model
for detection probability. However, I do not think the model for
detection probability tells you anything about how the covariates
influence true density. It only tells you how the covariates influence
detection probability and thereby influence the count data. You will need
to use linear regression or some other analysis to model your density
estimates as a function of your landscape/habitat variables.



What I do not know and would like to know is - if you find grass had a
negative influence on density after finding that grass also had a negative
influence on detection probability, can you draw any conclusions about the
relationship between grass and density? That is, will the effects of
grass on density be confounded with effects of grass on detection
probability, or will incorporation of detection probability into the
estimates of density factor out the influence of grass on detection
probability?



James Tucker





-----Original Message-----
From: Jeffrey Stratford [mailto:str...@AUBURN.EDU]
Sent: Wed 6/23/2004 12:27 PM
To: DISTANCE...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK
Cc:
Subject: [DIST-SAMP] density estimates and covariates



Distance-users,

I have point transect data with landscape parameters around each point
count stop and I used Distance to find the best-fitting detection model.
This top model has the covariate "%grass in a 100-m radius buffer
around each point". I would now like to fit a model that best predicts
per point density (I already have those estimates) using the same
landscape variables used to build the detection model. Does distance
perform this analysis or, and this would make me feel really dumb, does
the best detection model = best density model?

Many thanks,

Jeff

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: Reprise - density estimates and covariates
parts:
Yes, this is possible. The mcds modelling adjusts for the effect of the
covariate on detectability, but the resulting density estimates may well
be correlated with the same covariate. There is no reason why you
shouldn't model that relationship.

Steve Buckland
